source: https://github.com/cutelabnyc/cute-vcv (commit 98d7049, version 2.1.0-rev.0); the maker publishes no manual beyond https://shop.cutelab.nyc

lines: A pulsar synthesis oscillator: it fires a short grain of waveform on every cycle of its pitch, and the length, shape and rhythm of those grains are what you set
Sets the rate at which grains are fired, and so the pitch; it covers roughly 104Hz to 470Hz, or 13.75Hz to 3520Hz with the extended range button lit
Widens what the pitch knob covers, from a couple of octaves around the middle of the keyboard to eight octaves running from 13.75Hz to 3520Hz; it starts off and the lamp in it shows when it is on
Sets how long each grain is against the time between grains: short and separate anticlockwise, long and overlapping clockwise, which also opens the grain's bandwidth
Sets how deeply the internal modulator swings the grain length, none at the far left
Sets the rate of the internal modulator that swings the grain length, from a slow wobble at the far left up to audio rate; the lamp beside it follows that modulator
Ties the internal modulator's rate to the pitch, so the modulation tracks the note instead of holding a fixed speed, and it changes what the cadence and torque knobs cover; it starts off
Sweeps the waveform each grain is made of, crossfading in turn through a sinc, a triangle, a square, a saw, a contained square and a raw saw
Snaps the internal modulator's rate to a whole-number ratio of the pitch, so the modulation locks in step instead of drifting against it; it starts off
Moves the grain length, five volts covering half the travel of the density knob, and it is added to wherever that knob is set
Moves the grain waveform, five volts covering the whole travel of the shape knob, and it is added to wherever that knob is set
Moves the modulation depth, five volts covering the whole travel of the torque knob, and it is added to wherever that knob is set
Moves the modulation rate, five volts covering the whole travel of the cadence knob, and it is added to wherever that knob is set
Scales how much the linear FM jack bends the pitch, one volt giving the depth this jack has with nothing patched; a cable resting at 0V therefore shuts linear FM off
Bends the pitch by a fifth of itself per volt at an index of one, so the shift keeps its proportion as the pitch changes rather than staying a fixed number of hertz
Sets the pitch at a volt per octave, added to the pitch knob
While this is above 2.5V the oscillator is held at the start of its cycle, so an edge restarts it and a gate held high stops it dead until the gate falls
The pulsar oscillator itself, the train of grains the module is set up to make
A square wave at the pitch the module is running at, 10V for the first half of each cycle and 0V for the second, whatever the grains are doing
Note — every jack takes polyphony, and the number of voices the module runs is the largest channel count arriving at any of the eight of them
Note — the module sounds the moment it is placed; the pitch knob starts a quarter of the way up, at about 151Hz, and every other control starts at its minimum

mom-jeans.notes: The panel prints pulsar and square over the two output jacks while the maker's tooltips call them Output and Trigger; the lines follow the panel, and square is the more accurate of the two names, because that jack carries a 50 per cent square wave at the pitch rather than a trigger pulse. The sync jack is read as a level every sample and not as an edge, so a gate held above 2.5V pins the oscillator at the start of its cycle for as long as it is held. FM INDEX is normalled to 1, so patching it with a cable at 0V removes linear FM rather than adding to it. The extended-range button carries no printed label. The sum ranges are written as the voltage the knob-plus-jack total is worth, since the clamp itself is on an internal ratio. The pitch figures are worked out from the code: the knob maps its travel onto MIDI note 23 to 49, or -12 to 84 with extended range on, and the frequency is 27.5 times two to the power of the note over twelve, clamped to 1Hz and 20000Hz. The only context menu is a light, dark and Halloween panel choice, which is cosmetic and gets no line. Commit 98d7049 is the only one carrying version 2.1.0-rev.0, its plugin.json is byte-identical to the installed one and its res/ matches the installed artwork file for file.
